Not a party with a stay-reason that needs a seat; building “for the agent” as a persona would invent a user World did not acquire. |

---

## 3. The operator/house layer — shape, membership, and surfaces

### Shape decision

**House-global console + per-tenancy admin.**

- **House-global console** — cross-firm: Approach/ads, shared immigration reference data, methodology/Register evolution (build tooling), platform-level packs and template libraries, activation/forward-deploy pipeline, cross-firm oversight, founder/agency controls, operator audit of house actions, customer-support queue.
- **Per-tenancy admin** — one firm at a time: intentional provision (assisted door), escrow/commercial posture for that firm, which evaluation and engagement operations are bound under that firm’s identity, reachability/audit of that book, firm-scoped health of sequences, support context for that firm’s running state.

**Why this split from World’s ecosystem.** One agency runs many tenancies; the firm inhabits the book and meetings while the house configures and oversees the operations that run eligibility and engagement. Cross-firm functions (ads supply, versioned public-reference tables, product regeneration) have no natural home inside a single firm’s admin. Per-firm operations (provision this tenancy, arm this firm’s campaign, hold this firm’s contingent terms) have no natural home in a purely global wall. A single operator surface would blur those jobs; the split matches the agency shape World already stated.

### 8. Fact-refresh / data-collection

**Must fulfill:** Use touchpoints as the data-collection mechanism; route answers by field class; write back into eligibility.

**The system must be able to:**

- Fire nudges that ask for or infer facts affecting eligibility (`Seed §5.4`; `World §0.4`).
- Classify fields and route:
  - **Self-reportable** → forms / pre-meeting capture.
  - **Document-dependent** → **never** a form; tracked work items.
  - **Employer-directed** → ask the **firm**, not the client (`Seed §5.4`; `World §0.4`).
- Accept answers from the client or consultant hand-entry; on any write-back, initiate **immediate re-evaluation** (`Seed §5.8`).
- Record a *missing* fact as a signal (Engine 2 input) (`Seed §5.8`).

**Must not:** Put document-dependent needs into forms (`Seed §5.4`).

**Chains to:** Every write-back triggers Eligibility; missing facts feed Engine 2 (`Seed §5.8`).

**Silences:** Client desk depth (touchpoint-only vs authenticated portal) (`Seed §13.4`); D-02 in-meeting fallback surface (`Seed §5.8, §13.5`).

---

### 9. Reference-currency

**Must fulfill:** Keep IRCC-shaped reference facts current as versioned data, with no code deploy.

**The system must be able to:**

- Maintain versioned reference tables (categories, trades, cutoffs, provincial identifiers, etc.) as **data** (`Seed §5.7`; `World §1.3, §2.2.1`).
- Treat a reference move (draw threshold/cutoff shift, category added, trade/provincial identifier change) as a **faceless** first-class trigger — no screen, no human click (`Seed §5.7`; `World §2.2.1`).
- Hold industry criteria packs (Constants) as versioned packs; V1 truth is Canada-shaped (`Seed §5.6, §2.6`).

**Must not:** Require a code deploy to update reference facts (`Seed §5.7` Directive 3).

**Chains to:** A reference change triggers Eligibility re-evaluation for every affected contact — the **law / public-reference** side of detection (`World §2.2`).

**Silences:** Ownership / IP / liability of rule packs (`Seed §13.9`; `World §1.2`); Constants packs beyond Immigration (`Seed §13.16`).

---

### 10. Eligibility re-evaluation

**Must fulfill:** Recompute private service eligibility when client facts or reference move; emit every determination as a signal.

**The system must be able to:**

- Evaluate from firm-held + engagement-collected client facts against house-held / firm-configured rules — **private** to the firm book (`Seed §2.4`; `World §0.4`).
- Accept two detection sides: (1) law/public-reference moves, (2) life-change facts only the person/firm-file knows (`World §2.2`).
- Run the automation shape: Trigger (scoped pull — manual rich; event thinner) → Constants → Conditions → Rules → structured output → downstream resolution (`Seed §5.6`; `World §0.4, §2.3`).
- Treat pathway pass as **any** pathway assertion (CEC **or** FSW **or** FST **or** PNP-*), not one favoured pathway (`Seed §5.7` Directive 2; `World §0.4`).
- Produce an **Analysis** readout (headlines, deltas, service candidates, nudge/reactivation hints) with machine output retained underneath (`Seed §5.7`; `World §0.4`).
- Emit **every** determination — including missing-data — as a signal (`Seed §5.8`).
- Keep evaluation inspectable/changeable without deploy (open-box / house layer) (`World §3.4, §2.1`).

**Must not:**

- Cold-detect strangers’ immigration eligibility from public databases as Core Function (`Seed §2.4, §14`; `World §0.4`).
- Treat a static book dump as sufficient for the life-change side (`World §2.2`).

**Chains to:** Every emitted signal triggers Engine 2 (`Seed §5.8`).

**Silences:** Operations & Actions initiation law (stubs) (`Seed §5.6, §11`); event-trigger set (`Seed §5.6, §11`); Rules UI toggles vs condition trees (`Seed §13.13`); workflow persistence target (`Seed §13.12`).

---

### 11. Signal / motion orchestration (Engine 2)

**Must fulfill:** Record every detection; choose the single outbound motion by fixed precedence.

**The system must be able to:**

- Record every detection — including missing data — as a **signal** when found (`Seed §5.8`; `World §0.4`).
- Decide outreach separately from recording, under fixed precedence (`Seed §5.8`):
  1. **Reactivation first**, whenever anything is reactivation-worthy.
  2. **Nudge only** when nothing is reactivation-worthy.
  3. When a nudge fires, consolidate **every** outstanding self-reportable need into **one** form — never one nudge per field.
  4. When reactivation fires, attach secondary signals as **agenda** on the consultant’s pre-meeting brief — never parallel outreach.
  5. **One client, one motion, ever** (`Seed §5.8, §16.11`; `World §3.3`).

**Must not:** Replace the attempt engine inside a sequence (`World §0.4`); fire parallel motions for one client (`Seed §5.8`).

**Chains to:** Chosen motion hands work to Engagement (reactivation or nudge sequence) (`Seed §5.8`; `World §3.3`).

**Silences:** What makes a signal **reactivation-worthy** (`Seed §5.8`); D-01 / D-02 builder placement (`Seed §5.8, §13.5`).

---

### 12. Meeting / loop-closer

**Must fulfill:** On meeting booked, close the loop with pending capture and a live brief.

**The system must be able to:**

- Treat **meeting booked** as the core success / loop-closer event (`Seed §4, §5.8`).
- On `meeting_booked` with outstanding self-reportable fields, open a data-capture form pending the meeting (`Seed §5.8`; `World §0.4`).
- On any write-back against that capture (or consultant entry), run **immediate re-evaluation** (`Seed §5.8`).
- Keep the pre-meeting brief **live** (recomputed), not a snapshot (`Seed §5.8`; `World §0.4`).

**Chains to:** Write-backs re-trigger Eligibility, keeping the brief current (`Seed §5.8`).

**Silences:** D-01 — pre-meeting capture as tail of reactivation vs standalone `meeting_booked` sequence; D-02 — in-meeting fallback module (`Seed §5.8, §13.5`).

---

## Cross-system trigger web

Initiations where one system's output is another's trigger:

| From | Trigger event | To |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Acquisition | seed inputs land | 2 Provision |
| 3 Commercial | hard inputs land / campaign **running** | Application desk open (5–12) |
| 5 Audit | sequence-ready verdict | 7 Engagement enrollment |
| 7b Attempt | finishing event | 7 arms next sequence |
| 7 Engagement | nudge touchpoint fires | 8 Fact-refresh (data ask) |
| 8 Fact-refresh | write-back | 10 Eligibility |
| 9 Reference-currency | reference move | 10 Eligibility |
| 10 Eligibility | every determination (incl. missing) | 11 Engine 2 (signal) |
| 11 Engine 2 | chosen motion | 7 Engagement (reactivation / nudge) |
| 12 Meeting | meeting_booked → capture write-back | 10 Eligibility (live brief) |

**Spine shape:** *seed → forward-deploy → run*, then a self-feeding *detect → engage → collect → re-detect* ring, with Reference-currency injecting faceless external triggers into the ring (`World §2.2`).

---

## Hard human gates (machine must not automate these away)

From `Seed §9` / `World §4`:

- Seed capture (stranger action)
- Firm/user provision (OLG) and OTP verify
- Database authorization
- Escrow accept
- Client opt-in / not silenced
- Meeting booking (human commitment)
- Firm responsibility to refuse illegal/unethical outreach

---

## Silences master list (not filled)

| Silence | System |
|---|---|
| Escrow release definition | 3 |
| Shape of database authorization | 3 |
| Ongoing SaaS packaging vs escrow peer door | 3 |
| Email earns Meta entry; Meta CAC | 1 |
| CASL/SMS consent regimes | 6, 1 |
| Reactivation-worthy criteria | 11 |
| Attempt criteria windows (product lock) | 7b |
| SMS reply-failure escalation | 7b |
| Event-trigger set; Operations & Actions stubs | 10 / stubs |
| Import fully mutates living list | book → 5 |
| D-01 / D-02 loop-closer builder | 12, 11 |
| Client desk depth | 8, 12 |
| Multi-consultant roles | 4 |
| Rule-pack IP/liability; Constants beyond Immigration | 9, 10 |

---

## What this Story is for next

1. **Founder challenge** this substance — missing musts, false musts, silences wrongly filled.
2. **Systems Requirements** = **spec extraction** from these statements (states, transitions, ramifications, extrusion index late) — not a second invention pass. See [`SYSTEMS-REQUIREMENTS.md`](./SYSTEMS-REQUIREMENTS.md).
3. Faces (controls / panes) bind only after Requirements name the states these musts imply.

## Law of the face (short)

1. **Sequence is blank.** An agent sequence is a container. It can hold **multiple goals** (multiple campaigns). Not one-objective-or-nothing.
2. **Two objectives → two campaigns.** If you want two things met, each requires its own campaign. When a campaign’s **objective is met**, you may string the next campaign. There is **no “first objective”** object. The distance between campaigns is **not** a qualify node.
3. **Opt-in (the teaching example):** **Launch window** and **Launch day** are **campaign names** we used so the first pictures had something in them. The operator can rename both. Window builds desire (why we don’t start at reactivation). Launch day, in that example, is opt-in day. That pair is **not** a frozen system type.
4. **Campaigns have objectives. Channels do not.** Channels are the **medium**. **Channel rules = escalation on that medium** (not opened, not clicked, …). **Attempt rules are not at the channel.** An attempt is a **container / cycle** of the same sequence.
5. **Sequencing lives at campaign level** (“how many channels here, in what order”) — not at the channel node.
6. **Content lives inside the channel node** as an **Override content toggle**. On → the node **expands** to contain that medium’s content-creation block (SMS composer, email composer, call script). Not a wired sibling. Not a small button. Attempt-specific copy is a **variation on that same node**.
7. **Override this** is the first toggle on a campaign. It **opens the campaign** and **reveals channel nodes as wires**. Campaign-level toggles **stay on the campaign**. Open a channel → **channel rules** (escalation) hang off as the channel’s deeper grain. Content stays inside.

## Law of the face (short)

1. **Agents (creation place) is left complete enough.** Operator authors **campaigns** there. Automations is the **brain / operations**. Do not grow Agents to invent forms.
2. **Automations shape (definite middle):** **On this event** (schedule or trigger) → **perform this operation** (the middle does not change; it is definite) → **on this kind of result do X / on that kind do Y**. Results are **binary** (or the binaries we have defined). More **DAG-like** than Agents’ sequence canvas.
3. **Exit points** sit at the **end of that operation**, per instance that ran.
4. **Re-engagement is not an objective.** It is a **campaign** (the name of a campaign). Already Agents law: opt-in / re-engagement / reactivation are **sequence templates**. An automation does not “trigger a re-engagement objective.”
5. **What an automation typically originates** is a **data request** objective — fill this form with these questions — **not** “click this button.” Maybe other objective types. Click-this still lives on **Agents** (launch window). Automations would not trigger it.
6. **The form is created in Automations.** Agents is not about creating forms or creating what is needed. Agents is about **sending people to accomplish the goal**. How Automations works the form has nothing to do with Agents.
7. **Recursive join:** a **data request is already an event of origin for Agents**. Data request = a form, handled by Automations. The Automations **end node** (start / select an agent) **mirrors** the Agents **beginning** (declare the objective).
8. **Same end node (leaning embedded):** assign an agent **or** instantiate from a template, **and** declare the objective right there. If that objective is a data request, **create the form in that same node**. Form-as-its-own-graph-node vs embedded-with-calling-the-agent is **not locked** — founder leans **embedded**. **00:02:** you do **not** author a new agent in this module (law 31).
9. **Select an agent = the whole sequence.** Campaigns live **inside** sequences. No separate campaign picker on that node. Campaigns can be templated. **Which agents you may select is limited by the objective** — can be enforced.
10. **Automation may trigger creation of a campaign** when a **templated** campaign already exists for that objective. That is enroll / instantiate, not Agents growing a form builder.
11. **Hub is the complete Automations module.** Current-app / CT Ant Automations was **born from Hub**. It is a **translation** (same kind) and a **poor rendition of quality**. Work from Hub nodes. Do not “fix” Ant independently as if it were the source.
12. **Look at Rules to see the end goal.** Plate: Hub → Automations → **New firm → opt-in launch** → Rule **Immigration · Service eligibility**. Open it: **toggles** on outcome families (Pathway detection, Gaps, Profile & operations, Category draws, Draw competitiveness). Under the hood: conditions against constants. A **rule is a composite of conditions and constants**. Rules are **creatable**. Modular **across industries**.
13. **Easy to miss because it touches more of the app.** Something comes in (outreach, existing data, other sources) → perform an operation → **actions are not only outreach**. Outcomes also **change stuff inside the system**.
14. **Not limited to code.** PM verdict: the authored logic **is simple enough for a GUI**. A condition is field · operator · constant. A rule is togglable families of those. Under-the-hood evaluator stays code. **Two options:** **GUI** (default where possible) · **Custom** (code / JSON when the GUI isn’t enough).
15. **Smallest workflow = trigger · rule · action.** A rule lets us create the smallest looking automation. Then name the pieces and build them separately.
16. **This Rule part does not exist in the Ant translation.** Image mocks are **from scratch** in Ant chrome. Mock = generate the image. See [`AUTOMATIONS-UI-BLUEPRINT.md`](./AUTOMATIONS-UI-BLUEPRINT.md).
17. **Inside a rule, outcomes can be GUI or named code.** Where a constant can be referenced, GUI (prefer always defining a constant when possible). Where no constant can be referenced — especially across industries — it is **named code** (JavaScript or Python), **created in the rules module**, not hard-coded. It still **toggles on or off**. You name it. Side-by-side with GUI outcomes. (Whole-rule Custom/JSON remains the escape hatch for the entire rule.)
18. **Look inside trigger and inside action.** Add a node, select Action as a node. Not satisfied with canvas-only.
19. **At least two kinds of actions:** (a) **in the application** — change something inside the system from the operation; (b) **agents** — send people to a goal.
20. **Agents as the action:** select an agent, or create / select the objective. Creating the objective probably **creates the form** (already Automations-owns-the-form).
21. **A rule can emit re-engagement and/or reactivation as signals — one, the other, or both at once.** Do not split the rule to separate them. That is why we can have **different actions**. Engine 2 already: every detection is a signal; outreach is one motion (reactivation first; nudge only if not; secondary attaches as agenda).
22. **Rule output classes are a lattice.** They all need to exist. Each class is something you can put a simple **condition** on, and that **forks actions** — including three kinds of actions on the **same data** (example: if re-engagement signal · if **only** re-engagement signal · if **anything other than that**).
23. **At least one class is missing: required data.** When the system knows data is required, that is a re-engagement signal **and** it must be an output class. Forms are built from that set — the questions **are** the required fields. Do **not** lock an objective type to a given signal; you can still create the objective.
24. **This loop is deterministic.** Seed already: collectible field class (self-reportable / document-dependent / employer-directed); every missing-data detection is a signal; nudge consolidates outstanding self-reportable needs into **one** form. No AI to decide what data is required. If that ever stops being true, say so.
25. **Required data as a class is a listing, not a flag — and it is not stood up.** The data being requested is **more than one** item. A catalog of collectible fields exists in code (`COLLECTIBLE_FIELDS`) and is **unused**. Rule-node output today is headline / pass / pathway & gap **result ids** / services / nudge & reactivation **signals** — not a list of requested fields. No UI lists that request. No form authoring **references** those ids. Contact forms that look like a list are painted demos. Until the listing is on rule output, a form cannot bind to it. Do not invent the rest of the catalog; do not mint tables.
26. **Two grains of condition. Do not collapse them.** Inside the rule: field · operator · constant (or named code). After the rule, on the DAG: a **condition / If node** that **calls from the previous result** (rule Output) and forks actions. Hub already has that If node. A10 / A13 are **diagrams of the lattice idea**, not a screenshot of that node, and not a screen to build. Founder 22:17: A13 is a different kind of picture.
27. **An event has a global grain and a local grain. That is not “Settings.”** Form completion **is** an event that can trigger an automation. **Global:** on all form submissions of that kind — whoever submitted, run this evaluation. **Local:** on **this** form — every time this specific form is submitted, run this evaluation. The same divide is why Automations needs a global/local place (it matches Agents’ global → sequence → campaign, without copying a Settings modal). This expands **what counts as an event**. Do not invent the rest of the event catalog this stamp. Do not call it Settings.
28. **No special return.** The return **is** an event. **All objectives are events.** The write-back **is** the event; the event happening **is** the write-back. It is detected across the app / in the database. It is not lost. Loop 1 (23:07) is settled this way — not a separate return wire.
29. **Lineage is queryable at the minimum.** What created the objective (agent-created or hand-created). The path that agent took from that creation to completion. The completion event. Time it took. Map it correctly. That is querying, not a new module. If it is not queryable, the loop is not real.
30. **Campaign failure is an event.** Global and local apply (all campaign failures vs **this** campaign). Then an **in-app action**: create a record — even as simple as **ascribe a tag**. ## After an action: the previous result is every write that run made

That is the primitive. It applies to every action. We do not specify a field list.

The action **passes the work to the real module**. When that module finishes, **every write that run made** is available to the next node. The next node **picks** which of those writes it is about.

Audit produces a lot of writes (the run, verdicts, sequence-ready, whatever else that run touched). All of that is available. Provision, given the form values, runs — every write from **that** run is available. Same shape.

“Two things” on Audit was a bad restatement. Two grains showed up because that module writes a batch row **and** per-person rows. That is the write-set. It is not a law that every action has two outputs.

**How you pick:** point the If at a write (or a field of a write) already on that handle. A person-row write splits people. A run-row write is the artifact.

**Not the previous result:** hearing the completion as a **trigger** on a different automation. That is the other door.

Hub `lastOutput` → `lastInput` is the smell, not the live path. Live is SA **015** (engineer). Do not recut it here.

## Shape: when a node finishes, you have what the module produced

This is the whole question. Automations only works if this is true.

An action is not a fake step. It **sends the work to the real module** (Audit, Contacts, Agents — whatever that action is). That module does its job, same as if you had pressed it on that desk.

When that node **completes**, the next step has **everything that module produced** — every write, every result — **as if you had done it in the module.** Naturally. Not a special automation-only copy. Not a guess.

Example: Audit action.

1. The node hands Audit **who we are auditing**.
2. Audit runs. It writes whatever that module writes.
3. After the node, **every write from that run** is the previous result. The next node picks. Not a short list we specified.

Same for Provision: this form submitted → pass the values → every write from that provision run.

### Two layers. That is the whole shape.

| Layer | What it is |
|-------|------------|
| **The writes** | Live in the module. **Every write that run made.** Same records you would open on that desk. Not a shadow copy Automations invented. |
| **The handle** | After this node, the next step is pointing at **those** writes — not “go find some audit.” The next node **picks** which write. |

A wire that looks like an n8n **pipe** is one way to see the handle. A then-this list where the next node reads **this node’s output id** is the same product. **Pipe vs this-then-that is not the question.** The question is: when the node completes, do we have the module’s output. If the next step has to guess (latest audit for this firm), it is not this node.

“Everything it produces” means **every write that run made**. Not a short list. Not the entire database from other runs. The If is calling from **that**.

### Two doors. Do not collapse them.

| Door | What it is |
|------|------------|
| **On this canvas** | Event → Audit action → If on that output → tag / agents. Needs the **handle**. |
| **A different automation** | Hear **audit finished** as an event (Global / Local). That is a listen. It is not a substitute for the handle on this canvas. |

- **Live walk** (`workflowWalk`): Trigger → … → Action. Action is enroll / call_agent. It does not send work to Audit. It does not hand the next node Audit’s run. Context is trigger payload + contact ids — not “what this node’s module just wrote.”

If the live walk cannot see the module’s output after the node, Automations does not work.

# Systems — change packet 022 (Objective met is a Local event)

**Seat:** Systems Analyst.
**When:** 2026-08-21 09:30 UTC.
**What this is:** the cut that makes **“this sequence ran, the objective is met”** the same mechanism as a Local trigger. Implementer **only implements**. No analysis left.
**Why:** Founder: events/triggers already have a solid mechanism underneath — a write we designated as a trigger. Objective met must have that same underneath. *“This specific form is filled and submitted by this user… back into the system, so the system can detect it and say: oh, they submitted this form — what’s that sequence?”* That mapping-and-matching is this packet.
**Join:** 010 housing (`campaign`, `campaign_objective`) · 017 `event_write_set` / `event_test_data` · A26 Local axes (`triggerLocalRefFromPayload` / `triggerLocalAxesMatch`) · [`PRIMITIVES.md`](./PRIMITIVES.md) row **“An objective was met”** · [`SYSTEMS-GOAL.md`](./SYSTEMS-GOAL.md) · flagship [`PHASE-TWO-LOG.md`](./PHASE-TWO-LOG.md) **15:43**.
**Flag:** 15:43 untouched. **Do not recut 015 / 019.** **#108 merged** (`018_collectible_fields.sql`). This is the next cut.
**UI:** none required. Founder: the UI that exists is all the UI this needs. This is backend.
**Instructions:** founder only.

---

## 1. The mechanism, stated once

A Local event today is **two** things, and Tower already has both:

1. A **write** we designated as a trigger (event = the INSERT — law 1).
2. An **instance axis on that row**, so “this one” is answerable — not just “one of these happened.”

`contact_import` is Local because `contact_records.import_batch_id` **is a column**. `campaign_failure` is Local because `campaign_failure.campaign_id` **is a column**. The matcher (`triggerLocalAxesMatch`) then tests only the axes the operator specified.

**Objective met is exactly that shape.** The completion write **is** the event. Nothing new is needed conceptually.

**And the axis comes from a binding.** When the operator picks the objective on the Automations Action, they are **binding** that objective to something concrete — the column is already called `action.payload_binding`. Authorship binds; the runtime carries that binding out on the wire (§2.1) so the return leg can be matched. The stamp is not new information — it is the binding, made physical. §2.6 decides what it binds to.

What is missing is only (2) — **the completion rows do not carry which campaign asked for them:**

| Objective kind | Completion write (010) | Instance axis on the row today | Local possible? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meeting` | `meeting_booked` | `enrollment_id` (no FK) | **Nearly** — enrollment, not objective |
| `form` | `fact_writebacks` | **none.** `form_ref` is passed in the dispatch payload and **never persisted** (`004` has no such column) | **No** |
| `click` | `messaging_events` → `outbound_messages` | **none.** No enrollment / campaign / attempt column anywhere on the send | **No** |

That is the entire gap. It is not philosophical and it is not a missing Story must. **Two of the three objective kinds cannot be matched back to the sequence that asked.**

And so the current met-check is Global-shaped where it must be Local-shaped:

```
campaignHousing.campaignObjectiveMet()
  → SELECT 1 FROM <completion_table> WHERE firm_id=$1 AND contact_id=$2 LIMIT 1
```

**Any** meeting this person ever booked, **any** fact they ever submitted, **any** message event at all satisfies **any** campaign objective. A meeting booked last quarter completes today’s launch window. That is the bug the founder is pointing at.

**The fix is two halves: stamp the ask, then match the answer.**

---

## 2. Hard decisions

### 2.1 Stamp the ask (outbound carries the objective)

When a sequence deploys outreach **in pursuit of an objective**, the objective rides on what goes out. This is what makes the return leg matchable.

```sql
-- Sends carry the pursuit.
ALTER TABLE outbound_messages
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS enrollment_id TEXT,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS campaign_id TEXT,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS campaign_objective_id TEXT,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS attempt_id TEXT;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS outbound_messages_objective_idx
  ON outbound_messages (campaign_objective_id, contact_id);

-- The form is per-objective. Persist the instance axis that the payload already carries.
ALTER TABLE fact_writebacks
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS form_ref TEXT,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS campaign_objective_id TEXT;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS fact_writebacks_objective_idx
  ON fact_writebacks (campaign_objective_id, contact_id);

-- Meeting already knows the enrollment. Name the objective too.
ALTER TABLE meeting_booked
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS campaign_objective_id TEXT;
```

No FK on these (TEXT tenancy, same posture as `meeting_booked.enrollment_id`; `campaign_objective` rows are firm-copied by `copySequence`). Nullable — a send outside a sequence (OTP, probe, house form) stamps nothing and is therefore never a completion.

# Systems — change packet 023 (Failure mode = stop spending, keep listening)

**Seat:** Systems Analyst.
**When:** 2026-08-21 09:50 UTC.
**What this is:** the cut for the failure mode that has been open since 2026-08-15 16:58. Implementer **only implements**.
**Why:** Founder: *“the failure mode is simple — it just means we're not gonna waste resources trying to make that objective happen. But if it happens, if it clears, then of course it's still a win… the objective is met.”*
**Join:** 022 (objective met is a Local event) — **read 022 first; this packet depends on its detect-on-the-write path.** 010 `campaign_failure` · `cascade.ts` ladder · [`SYSTEMS-OBJECTIVE-ESCROW.md`](./SYSTEMS-OBJECTIVE-ESCROW.md) (direction; not built).
**Flag:** 15:43 untouched. Do not recut 015 / 019. **#108 merged.** Cut 022 first.
**UI:** none required.
**Instructions:** founder only.

---

## 1. The law, stated once

Failure is **not** an ending. It is a **spending decision**.

| | Outbound (resources we spend) | Inbound (completion we listen for) |
|---|---|---|
| **Pursuing** | sends, attempts, channel ladder, escalation | listening |
| **Exhausted (failure mode)** | **stops** | **still listening** |
| **Nullified** (escrow era — not this packet) | stopped | **stops. The door refuses.** |

Two lines, not one. Exhaustion closes only the **outbound**. The objective stays claimable: if it clears later on its own, *“it still counts.”* Only **nullification** closes the inbound — and the only thing that nullifies is the firm pulling their money, which is [`SYSTEMS-OBJECTIVE-ESCROW.md`](./SYSTEMS-OBJECTIVE-ESCROW.md) and is **not built now**.

This is why 022 had to come first. Once detection happens **on the completion write** instead of inside the tick's open-attempt loop, closing attempts no longer blinds us. Before 022, "stop spending" and "keep listening" were the same switch. Now they are two.

## 2. The bug this fixes

`cascade.ts` (~533): when the channel ladder has no forward channel (`!toChannel`), it records `campaign_failure` and dispatches the event — then leaves `active_attempts.status = 'open'`.

So the tick picks that attempt up again. And again. Every subsequent due window with no forward channel writes **another** `campaign_failure` row and **re-dispatches** the event. That is:

- exactly the resource waste the founder is describing, and
- a duplicate-event bug — a workflow subscribed to `campaign_failure` fires repeatedly for one failure.

## 3. Hard decisions

### 3.1 Exhaustion is terminal for the attempt

```sql
-- 'exhausted' joins the existing status vocabulary.
-- DO NOT reuse 'nullified' — see 3.4.
UPDATE active_attempts
   SET status = 'exhausted', updated_at = now(),
       state = state || jsonb_build_object('exhausted_at', now()::text,
                                           'campaign_failure_id', $2::text)
 WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'open';
```

Cut in the `!toChannel` branch, immediately after `recordCampaignFailure`, **inside the same transaction as that INSERT** so a failure row can never exist with the attempt still open.

`campaign_failure` stays exactly one row per exhaustion, and `campaign_failure` dispatches exactly once.

The tick already selects `status='open'`, so an exhausted attempt drops out with no change to that query. No sends, no ladder, no escalation. Resources stop.

### 3.2 The pursuit is exhausted, not the enrollment

The attempt is spent; the **objective is not**. Record that on the cursor's pursuit so the desk can say why nothing is moving:

```sql
ALTER TABLE enrollment
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS pursuit_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pursuing'
    CHECK (pursuit_state IN ('pursuing', 'exhausted')),
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS exhausted_at TIMESTAMPTZ;
```

- Set `pursuit_state='exhausted'`, `exhausted_at=now()` when that enrollment's attempt exhausts.
- **Reset to `'pursuing'`, `exhausted_at=NULL` whenever `advanceEnrollmentCampaign` moves the cursor.** The next campaign is a fresh pursuit.
- `campaign_id` is **not** nulled by exhaustion. Only `advanceEnrollmentCampaign` (met) or the last campaign nulls it. Exhausted-with-a-cursor is the honest state: *we are not spending, we are still listening on this objective.*

Two states only. `met` is not a third — met **is** the cursor advancing (022 §2.3). Do not add it here.

### 3.3 Do not close the door

Explicitly forbidden on exhaustion, because each of these would silently kill the escrow angle:

- Do **not** null `enrollment.campaign_id`.
- Do **not** delete or advance past the `campaign_objective`.
- Do **not** `invalidate` / `consume` any `access_links` row, and do not disable a booking or form door.

**DNA for children (clause order):**
1. hand over my private book and authorize Tower to work under my license
2. eligible clients appear booked on my calendar without me setting up, configuring, or running engagement

---

## Depth 2a — hand over · authorize

**Q:** How do I hand over my private book and authorize Tower to work under my license?

**Clarity:** On Prepared Workspace, complete Authorize book (database grant or confirm import) and Accept terms (license + escrow). Those two commits are the hard inputs Activation state / Commercial read.

2. accept that outreach runs under my license and escrow

### Leaf 2a.1 — connect the book

**Q:** How do I connect my contact book?

On Authorize book modal, click Connect CRM / grant database access (or Upload / confirm assisted import), then click **Authorize** (primary button). That commit writes book-handover state read by Book readiness Audits and Activation state Progress (authorize-book row). When the assisted path already holds the list: Starting from Contacts, click **Imports**, click the imported batch row, and click **Confirm book for Tower** so the same handover state is set — without authoring sequences.

**Criteria — when:** During activation (ALG) or after assisted provision when the book must be confirmed.  
**Conditions:** Prepared Workspace is staged; Authorize book is available; or Contacts already holds the assisted import.

| Prepared Workspace | Module | shared / activation | **new** (activation artifact; not firm-nav chrome) | Activation shell |

---

### Leaf 2a.2 — authorize under license + escrow

**Q:** How do I accept that outreach runs under my license and escrow?

| Prepared Workspace | Module | shared / activation | **new** | Activation shell |

| Escrow terms | Block | consultant (accepts) / operator (holds) | **new** (operator Commercial oversees) | **View** panel of terms |

**Q:** How do eligible clients appear booked on my calendar without me setting up, configuring, or running engagement?

3. I never set up Automations, Agents, or engagement templates

## Open (tinkering — do not fill)

1. Full list of **operations** Automations performs (data request is one; engagement was spoken as a maybe).
2. Full list of **exit points** besides start/select agent.
3. Form creation: **own graph node** vs **embedded** in the start-agent node (lean: embedded).
4. When an automation starts a campaign: **settled 00:02 / law 31.** Assign to an **existing** sequence, or **create from a template**. Do not create the agent in Automations.
5. Word “event” — **settled 23:35 / law 28:** all objectives are events. C2b and Automations triggers are the same grain. Do not split them again.

9. Remaining output classes besides **required data** (law 23). Do not invent a full catalog this stamp. Hub-today vs lattice is A9 / A10.
10. **Listing of requested data on rule output + form bind** (law 25). Named 21:36 as not stood up in code. Mocked as A11–A12 (chrome) and A13 (diagram). Do not fill the listing in the product this stamp. Do not mint tables.
11. **Ant plate of the If node** — **drawn 01:20:** A15 (chain) · A16 (open). Hub still has the plant. A13 is still not this screen.
12. **Event catalog + global vs local** (law 27). **Drawn 18:53: A18.** **Shape list (22:43):** [`PRIMITIVES.md`](./PRIMITIVES.md). Form submitted (this form) · campaign failed · opt-out · firm created · audit finished · contact file imported · objective met. Not “any row changed.”
13. **Queryable lineage** (law 29). Agent-created vs hand-created objective → path → completion → time. Minimum: queryable. Do not mint a table from this sentence.
14. **Handle after the node** (law 33). Live walk does not hand the next node the module’s output. Do not treat editor preview as that. SA: do not circle pipe vs then-this — both are fine if the handle is real. Packet: [`SYSTEMS-AUTOMATIONS-NODE-OUTPUT.md`](./SYSTEMS-AUTOMATIONS-NODE-OUTPUT.md).

**Today:** generated images. Beat 5 revised: content inside the node; attempt rules off the channel.

---

## Mock map (what you said → what you can see)

Not one picture. Five beats, one labeled mock. Objective is a **modal** on the canvas (same idea as Hub Add configuration). Sequence templates are their own beat because that picker is a different layer.

| Beat | What you said | Same mock or own |
|------|----------------|------------------|
| **1. Sequence templates** | Empty world; opt-in / re-engagement / reactivation are sequence templates, not objectives | Own beat (different picker) |
| **2. Add objective** | First thing on a campaign. Template (example names: launch window, launch day, additional) vs from scratch (click / calendar / form, then name it) | **Modal** on the canvas |
| **3. Two campaigns** | Two objectives → two campaigns. Distance = previous objective met (not a qualify node). In the example, Launch day = opt-in day | Canvas |
| **4. Override this** | First toggle. Reveals text / email / form as wires. Campaign toggles stay | Canvas |
| **5. Open a channel** | Channel rules (escalation) hang off. Content = button inside. Attempt rules are not here | Canvas expand |

Webhook / table lookup is named, not mocked. Call channel is not mocked.

---

## Objective first (binary event) — two template layers

Hub Automations (`/hub`): empty canvas → add a trigger → on that node, **Add configuration** (event configuration). Campaign authorship uses the same *seat*: the first thing on a campaign is the **objective**. That is not a license to put Automations triggers on the Agents canvas.

**From scratch:** the untemplated objective looks like an event (name may change). Everyone enrolled in this campaign is campaigned to do **one thing**. Yes or no. Then you name it.

| Spoken from-scratch | Binary |
|---------------------|--------|
| Click this link | Did they, or not |
| Book a meeting in this calendar | Did they, or not |
| Submit / complete this form | Did they, or not |
| Later: webhook / table (name in a list) | Did they, or not — do not mint now |

**From a template:** pick an **objective template** (a campaign, e.g. launch window). It populates everything related to that template. You do not pick “opt-in” here — that is a **sequence template**.

Empty world: no templates exist until authored. Keep that in the open.

---

## Further enrichment (agent alignment — not a second flag)

Founder: “I’m not circling, I’m enriching, and I think you can even further enrich.” This section is that enrichment. It does not replace 15:43 or the excerpts above.

**The agent is a sequence, not a campaign.** The list item (Opt-in, Nudge, Reactivation) is a **blank sequence**. Campaigns live inside it. Opt-in is the teaching case because it already needs **two** objectives, therefore **two** campaigns.

**Why a launch window exists (the meta-reason).** We do not start at reactivation. In the teaching example, the window’s job is to **build desire** for opt-in, and Launch day **is** opt-in day. Those are **names**. The next campaign is justified because the previous campaign’s **objective was met**. That is the 15:43 “goal is itself an escalation point” — the distance between campaigns, not a Settings row, not a fourth channel, and **not** a qualify node. The C3 pill was a founder caption. See [`IMAGE-CAPTION-AUDIT.md`](./IMAGE-CAPTION-AUDIT.md).

**One thing in the window.** Not the waitlist question. The window’s objective is still **one binary event** — everyone enrolled is campaigned to do that one yes/no. Spoken from-scratch for the window: probably **click this link**. Do not split the window into two campaigns unless there are two objectives.

**Two template layers.** Sequence templates = the full canvas (opt-in, re-engagement, reactivation). Objective templates = a single campaign (launch window, launch day, plus additional unnamed in opt-in). Empty world: no templates until authored. Keep that in the open.

**First thing on a campaign is the objective.** Same *seat* as Hub Automations (`/hub`): you add a trigger, then on that node **Add configuration**. Here you add a campaign, then the first thing on it is the objective. Do **not** put Automations triggers on this canvas.

**Untemplated objective = binary event** (the word “event” may change). Click this link · book this calendar · submit this form. Happened or it didn’t. Then you name it. Webhook / table lookup (name in a list → completed) is down the line; the system should not be so complicated that it is impossible. Do not mint that now.

**Toggle locality (law of the graph).** A toggle lives at the layer it governs and **does not migrate** when the graph opens.

| If the toggle is about… | It lives… | After Override this |
|-------------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| The campaign as a whole (sequencing, the objective, Override this) | On the campaign node | **Still on the campaign** |
| Escalation on that medium (channel rules) | Does not exist until the node exists | **Wired off the open channel** |
| Content for that medium | **Override content toggle** inside the channel node | On → node expands to the composer |
| Attempt (cycle count, gap after failed last node) | **Not the channel** | Attempt is a container around the sequence |

So Override this is not “show more fields on this card.” It **materializes the child layer**. The campaign stays. Channel nodes **hang off it on wires**. Open a channel → **channel rules** hang off; **content** stays inside as a **toggle** that expands the node.

**Channels are a sequencing method, not a goal layer.** Choosing how many channels, which, in what order **is** campaign sequencing. Channel rules = escalation on that medium. Attempt rules = parameters of the **cycle**, not of the medium.

**Content is inside the channel node.** **Override content** is a toggle. On → the node expands to the composer. Sequence / global content is possible (sequence Settings / Agents Settings). Attempt copy is a **variation on that same node** for that cycle.

**Closed campaign = accepting defaults** (sequence, then global). Open Override this only to author at the channel grain.

**Two Settings surfaces — same families, different grain.**

| Surface | Grain |
|---------|--------|
| **Agents Settings** | Global defaults for every rule family below |
| **Sequence Settings** | This sequence. Inherit from Agents unless overridden |

What belongs in both (the bunch, given everything said):

- **Attempt rules** — number of attempts; wait / distance after the failed last node; same sequence unless nth-attempt is different
- **Channel rules (escalation)** — per medium: text not opened / not delivered; email not opened / not clicked in time; form not submitted
- **Content** — per-medium defaults (possible at global and at sequence)
- **Sequencing** — default channel order (text → email → form)

Per-campaign attempt rules stay **on the campaign**. They do not appear as a strip in the middle of the sequence canvas.

**Deeper than a channel** for escalation is still a wire off that channel. Content is not that wire. Attempt rules are not that wire.

---

## What this is not

- Not overwriting the 15:43 flag.
- Not putting Automations **triggers** on this canvas. The Hub analogy is the **seat** (first thing on the node is configuration), not a copied trigger picker.
- Not treating “opt-in” as an objective template. Opt-in is a **sequence** template.
- Not minting webhook / table-query completion now. Named as possible later.
- Not restoring 14:58 “actions on goals” as a seventh list item — failure is **inside escalation**.
- Not putting **attempt rules** on the channel node. Attempt is a cycle of the sequence.
- Not hanging **content override** off the channel as a connected sibling. It is a **toggle inside** the node; on → the node expands to the content-creation block.
- Not assigning **objectives** to channels. Channels = medium + escalation rules.
- Not putting **sequencing** on the channel node. Sequencing = campaign.
- Spoken “call”: now on the face as a channel node (ElevenLabs). Machine still has form until Story/SA extract. Do not mint tables here.
- Not minting tables in this file. Table-first extract is SA, after Story promotion where needed. Modularity law still: if it can be overridden, it must be a row.
- Not creating **forms** here. A data-request form is Automations. Agents sends people to accomplish the goal. See [`AUTOMATIONS-FACE.md`](./AUTOMATIONS-FACE.md).
- Not putting enroll on **Publish**. Enroll is **Contacts** on that sequence (C8).
- Not treating C3’s “qualify — first objective met” as a node or a `qualify_gate`. Caption audit: [`IMAGE-CAPTION-AUDIT.md`](./IMAGE-CAPTION-AUDIT.md).
- Not treating the **engagement chart** as the lineage query. Those are two surfaces.

---

## Open (tinkering — do not fill)

1. Additional objectives inside the opt-in sequence besides launch window and launch day — unnamed.
2. What we call the untemplated objective (“event” vs another word).
3. May one sequence mix objective types in practice, or only “technically”?
4. Call via ElevenLabs — face only for now; machine still form.

# Data in tables — standing law

**Seat:** Founder → implementer (and Systems Analyst when the store is missing).  
**When:** 2026-08-19 18:44 UTC.  
**Flag:** [`PHASE-TWO-LOG.md`](./PHASE-TWO-LOG.md) **15:43 UTC** — do not overwrite.  
**Prior:** 2026-08-16 18:53 — seed the tables; do not seed data in the app. [`IMPLEMENTER-FACE-PASS.md`](./IMPLEMENTER-FACE-PASS.md). Table-first: [`system-map/BUILD-system-map-v2-table-inventory.md`](./system-map/BUILD-system-map-v2-table-inventory.md).  
**Cloud agents read this from** repo-root [`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md).

---

## The law

**Records that show inside a module come from tables.** A reasonable count of rows in the requisite tables — not a thick fake world, not an empty module.

**Never hard-code data into the app.** Not in a React table. Not in a painted empty-state that pretends there are people. Not a name, a tag, a verdict, a run, a firm, a contact baked into the component so the screen looks full.

When we **mint** a table or a field (and as we go, where that mint is already stood up): **populate the seed** (`supabase/seeds/`) so the module that reads it has records. The desk shows what the query returns.

Chrome can be specified. PM specifies the face. That is not a store.

If the **table** is missing, or the **field** is missing, or it is unspecified what to write — that is a **Systems Analyst** problem. Name it. **Do not build** until SA has ascribed what the row is, so you know what to do.

Do not invent the table in the SPA to finish the plate. Do not fill the plate with hard-coded rows while you wait.

| Lives here | Does not live here |
|------------|--------------------|
| Postgres tables · `supabase/migrations/` · `supabase/seeds/` | `src/app/**` UI components |
| Walker / wire **reading** those rows | Arrays of demo people inside a module |
| Stand-in ports only as a mirror of that shape when the wire is off | A second invented catalog in the client |

---

## Do not

- Hard-code data into the app.
- Mint a table from a picture.
- Recut 015. Overwrite 15:43. Plant.
- Paint Marita Patel (or anyone) into the SPA so Contacts is not empty.

**Kind:** secondary

Branding chrome is the firm's — not Om Coda's. Reachability was gated upstream by Book readiness; silenced contacts do not receive this send.

Either choice is valid; neither opens Configuration libraries.

### Implementation status (repo)

## Directive 1 — Wire the plumbing (bucket one)

2. Change **overall pathway pass**: pathway pass means **any** pathway result asserts (`R-CEC-01` **or** `R-FSW-01` **or** `R-FST-01` **or** `R-PNP-*`), **not** “CEC asserts.”

# Auth Service — Contract (Login OTP)

**Status:** Implemented (v0.3.1)  
**Aligns with:** `login` flow · `loginSendOtpStep.ts` · `loginVerifyOtpStep.ts`  
**Session decision:** **O-10 resolved — HTTP-only cookie** (`tower_session`). No session token in response body.

---

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Flow step | Purpose |
|--------|------|-----------|---------|
| `POST` | `/auth/otp/send` | 2–4, 9 | Issue OTP email |
| `POST` | `/auth/otp/verify` | 6–8 | Verify code, issue session cookie |
| `POST` | `/auth/otp/abandon` | — | Invalidate in-flight challenge (change email) |
| `GET` | `/auth/session` | — | Validate session for route guard |
| `POST` | `/auth/logout` | — | Clear session cookie + revoke row |
| `GET` | `/auth/register/status` | — | Register gate enabled + unlocked (internal) |
| `POST` | `/auth/register/unlock` | — | Verify `REGISTER_PASSWORD`, set gate cookie |
| `POST` | `/auth/register/lock` | — | Clear register gate cookie |

All paths are proxied from the Consultant Web App dev server (`/auth` → Auth Service on port 3001).  
On **Vercel**, the same paths are served by Serverless Functions via `vercel.json` rewrite (`/auth/*` → `/api/auth/*`).

---

## Session (O-10)

- Cookie name: `tower_session`
- Flags: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/`
- `Secure` in production (`NODE_ENV=production`)
- Value: opaque random token (32 bytes, base64url)
- Storage: `sessions.token_hash` = SHA-256(cookie value)
- **Step 8 wire:** `Set-Cookie` only — client does not read a token from JSON

---

## `POST /auth/otp/send`

**Request:** `{ "email": string }`

**Success `200`:**

```json
{ "ok": true, "message": "If that address is registered, we sent a verification code." }
```

Returned for **both** provisioned and unprovisioned emails (anti-enumeration).

**Ordering (sequential implementation of logical steps 3a–3d):**

1. Validate email format → `400`
2. Rate limit → `429` (see § Rate limits)
3. Log send attempt (`otp_send_log`)
4. Resolve tenancy: `SELECT users JOIN firms ON firm_id WHERE email = $1` (single query)
5. If no user → `200` generic (stop; no challenge, no Resend)
6. Invalidate prior challenges for `(firm_id, email)`
7. `INSERT otp_challenges` (commit)
8. `POST` Resend — on failure: mark `delivery_failed = true`, return `503`
9. On Resend success → `200`

**`503`:** `{ "ok": false, "error": "delivery_failed", "message": "We could not send the email. Try again shortly." }`

**`429`:** `{ "ok": false, "error": "rate_limited", "message": "Too many codes requested. Wait a few minutes and try again." }`

---

## `POST /auth/otp/verify`

**Request:** `{ "email": string, "code": string }`

**Success `200`:** `{ "ok": true }` + `Set-Cookie: tower_session=…`

**Ordering (sequential implementation of logical steps 7a–7b, one transaction):**

1. Validate → `400`
2. Resolve user (firm_id)
3. Begin transaction
4. `UPDATE otp_challenges SET consumed_at = now() WHERE … AND consumed_at IS NULL AND invalidated_at IS NULL AND delivery_failed = false AND expires_at > now() AND code_hash = $hash RETURNING *`
5. If no row → increment `verify_attempts` on latest active challenge if applicable → `401`

# Wire log — GO cutover (real ports)

**Status:** code cut over — **not** “prod E2E green”  
**Branch intent:** Resend CEM + Twilio SMS + Postgres CT stores + Resend webhooks

“Cut over” means client ports call `/wire` + `/auth` and server adapters exist. It does **not** mean:

## 5. Core loop (application mechanics — dense)

```
Contacts / import
  → Audit (reachability / sequence-start gate)
  → Standard engagement sequence (opt-in → re-engagement nudges → …)
  → Collect & refresh Client Data via touchpoints
  → Rule engine / Automations (re-evaluate eligibility — R-* / B-* / Analysis)
  → Nudges / escalations / reactivation / consultant signals
  → Meeting booked (loop-closer — see Engine 2)
  → (repeat as facts & rules move)
```

### 5.1 Contacts enter the book

- Sources: CRM export, spreadsheet, lead list, manual add.
- Prototype: Contacts sidebar + CSV import UX; **CSV does not fully mutate** the living list yet (honesty).
- Channels matter: email and/or phone must be usable for the intended sequence channel.

### 5.2 Audit (Hub → Audits)

**Operational question only:**

> Can we reach this contact, and can we start a sequence on them?

Audit runs against **imports / the book** as **data-validity checks** (email valid, phone valid, channel match to the intended sequence, dedupe, already-in-Tower, consent/silenced, name present) — not pathway scoring and not sales ROI. Checks are intended to connect to **external validation systems** where needed. The job is to make contacts **sequence-ready** for Agents / Automations.

| In scope | Out of scope (not Audit) |
|----------|---------------------------|
| Email valid, phone valid, ≥1 reachable channel matching sequence | Pathway / CRS scoring |
| Typo/garbage, dedupe, already-in-Tower, consent/silenced, name present | Activation probability / ROI forecasts |
| Open reachability issues as Hub meta | Minimum contact-count gates; sales PASS/FAIL ceremony |

**Verdicts (conceptual):** Reachable / Partial / Unreachable.  
**Secondary benefit:** Dirty list teaches the firm their DB is stale — byproduct, not the engine.  
**Sales vs product:** External “Database Opportunity Assessment” HTML is **marketing**. In-app Audit must feel **operational**.

Shape bets (open-box Hub, eventual agency view): [`OPERATOR-REVISIONS.md`](./OPERATOR-REVISIONS.md).

### 5.3 Engagement phases (product model)

| Phase | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| **Opt-in** | Firm → client; consent and first channel open |
| **Re-engagement (nudges)** | Ongoing touchpoints; collect and refresh data |
| **Reactivation** | Re-engage dormant / quiet contacts when rules or data warrant |

**Board phase language (prototype):** opt-in, re-engagement, reactivation; also silenced / opted-out indicators; reactivation can be **armed** (ghost template ready) vs **active** (sequence executing).

**Contact indicators (prototype):** sequenced / silenced / unsequenced (silenced when not opted in).

### 5.4 Nudges are not spam — they are the data collection mechanism

Each touchpoint can ask for or infer facts that affect eligibility: work history, language, permit expiry, province, job change, EE profile freshness, ECA status, etc.

**Collectible field classification (settled law):**

| Flag | Meaning | Downstream |
|------|---------|------------|
| **Self-reportable** | Client knows offhand (scores, dates, statuses) | Eligible for forms / pre-meeting capture |
| **Document-dependent** | ECA reports, LMIA paperwork, employer revenue, etc. | **Never** enter a form; become tracked **Manage** items |
| **Employer-directed** | Ask is aimed at the **firm**, not the client | Separate routing |

### 5.5 Agents (Hub → Agents)

- Author **sequences**: ordered steps of channel + copy (email, SMS, tasks today; extensible).
- Reactivation / launch agents are **composites** of those steps.
- Automations **select / enroll** agents as actions when criteria match (How: Automations trigger reactivation agent when criteria met).
- Agent composer is config UI; runtime send is automation/Wiring.

**Two sequencing layers (don’t conflate):**

1. **Campaign day calendar** (opt-in / reactivation content order) — `guidelines/Reactivation.md`.
2. **Attempt / channel-ownership engine** (what Sarah’s nudge shows: Text → Email → Form, Attempt 1/2/3 under the owner that failed, criteria windows, forward-only handoff) — reference story in `src/app/data/sarahNudgeTimeline.ts`; laws in [`OPERATOR-REVISIONS.md`](./OPERATOR-REVISIONS.md) §5b and `docs/product/engagement-chart-gantt-decisions.md`. Authored in Agents; Activity is the event record only.

### 5.6 Automations (Hub → Automations) — peer modules

Product model (not nested under Rules):

| Module | Role |
|--------|------|
| **Trigger** | Starts run; pulls scoped records (manual rich; event thinner) |
| **Constants** | Industry criteria (Immigration rich; Legal / Financial / Insurance placeholders) — versioned packs; segment swap bet |
| **Conditions (If)** | Branch gate; AND/OR; true/false pass-through |
| **Operations** | Transform/compute — stub |
| **Rules** | Pre-packaged evaluators over constants + industry conditions; Immigration · Service eligibility → R-* / deltas / B-* + Analysis (open box, not sealed) |
| **Actions** | Downstream side effects — stub |

**Canonical flow:** Trigger pulls → Rule and/or If evaluate → structured output → downstream nodes resolve `lastInput` (branch-aware).

**Manual trigger:** applies-to data classes/scopes, filters, enrollment summary, play/stop against pulled rows.

**Shape bet:** same graph + new Constants/Rules pack ≈ new vertical with a similar firm-book shape; evaluation stays inspectable (agency/operator view is the intended eventual home — today Hub sits in the firm workspace). See [`OPERATOR-REVISIONS.md`](./OPERATOR-REVISIONS.md).

### 5.7 Eligibility / immigration matrix (product claim)

- Outcome families (pathway, gaps, ops, category, draw) toggled in Rule config — not primarily hand-wired condition graphs in the primary UI.
- Pathway pass = **any** pathway assertion (CEC **or** FSW **or** FST **or** PNP-*), not CEC-only (Directive 2 law).
- Reference tables (categories, trades, cutoffs, OINP IDS, etc.) are **versioned data Tower maintains** — no code deploy to update (Directive 3).
- Analysis pane: human-readable headlines, nudge/reactivation hints, B-* services, narratives, deltas; JSON retained for power users.

**Fields that unlock gaps/ops (examples):** `eca_status`, `ee_profile_exists`, `ee_profile_last_updated`, `foreign_work_years`, plus existing language/TEER-style gates, CRS/draw constants.

### 5.8 Engine 2 law — signal / action (settled; orchestration open)

Every detection — including **missing-data** — is recorded as a **signal** when found. Outreach is decided separately by fixed precedence:

1. **Reactivation first, always** if anything is reactivation-worthy.
2. **Nudge only** when nothing is reactivation-worthy.
3. When a nudge fires, consolidate **every** outstanding self-reportable need into **one form** — never one nudge per field.
4. When reactivation fires, secondary signals attach as **agenda** to the consultant’s **pre-meeting brief** — no parallel outreach.
5. **One client, one motion, ever.**

**Loop-closer (behavior settled; builder open):**

- On `meeting_booked` with outstanding self-reportable fields → data-capture form pending the meeting.
- Write-back (form or consultant entry) → **immediate re-evaluation**.
- Brief is **live**, not a snapshot.

**Open decisions:**

- **D-01:** Pre-meeting capture = tail of reactivation sequence vs standalone `meeting_booked` sequence.
- **D-02:** Which module is the in-meeting fallback surface for unresolved form gaps.

### 5.9 Consultant visibility surfaces (application)

| Surface | Job |
|---------|-----|
| **Board** | Client list, phase signals, entry to client |
| **Client Data** | Profile, Q&A, forms, eligibility-related facts |
| **Activity / Journey / engagement chart** | Timeline of touchpoints, escalations, armed/active states |
| **Contacts** | Directory + indicators; import |
| **Hub** | Audits, Agents, Automations (and related workspace tabs e.g. constants) |
| **Login** | Passwordless OTP marketing/app entry |

### 5.10 Auth & tenancy (application / OLG path)

- Firms + users enter via **versioned seed manifests** only (no ad hoc SQL) — assisted onboarding / bootstrap.
- Passwordless OTP: send → verify → `tower_session` HttpOnly cookie.
- Unprovisioned emails: **generic 200**, no code (anti-enumeration).
- Session validation for route guard; logout clears cookie.
- Register gate (`REGISTER_PASSWORD`) is **internal Om Coda tooling**, not product chrome for firms.

---

## 6. ALG lattice (growth — dense)

### 6.1 Definitions (corrected)

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Acquisition** | Obtain **seed inputs** required to *provision*, from a stranger, autonomously, within click budget. Ends when seed inputs land. |
| **Activation** | Systemize path from provisioned stranger → **last inputs required to run**. Includes forward-deploy and earning hard inputs. Ends when campaign can run. |
| **Application** | Desk/product performing Core outcome once running. |
| **Running** | After last activation input; campaign performs without asking for more *required* activation inputs. |
| **Evolution** | Product changes from running-client feedback through Register passes (a friction becomes a documented gap, then a written affordance or backend facet, then regenerates into the product). Not a client lifecycle phase. |
| **Approach** | Acquisition strip of surfaces: feed → ad → capture → continue scroll (entry surfaces are product surfaces). |
| **Agentic acquisition** | Self-managing ads later — **not** required for ALG. Hand-built ads + automated post-click is still ALG. |

**Growth models (same input set; different supplier):**

- **OLG/SLG** — operator collects inputs (call / assisted).
- **PLG** — persona fills forms themselves.
- **ALG** — cheap public seed given; system extrapolates / forward-deploys; agent earns hard inputs mid-activation.

We had been wrongly attributing activation work to acquisition. **Activation sets the target; acquisition fulfills the seed quota.**

### 6.2 Acquisition input contract (finish line)

| Input | Notes |
|-------|--------|
| Name (firm / consultant) | Public / freely given |
| Website | Public |
| Phone **or** email | Channel for agent follow-up |

**Channel V1:** Meta (Facebook / Instagram). LinkedIn deferred.  
**Click budget:** stranger → these inputs only. Force at **one click** as design constraint; relax only as a finding. Easier to add clicks than remove.  
**Approach strip:** feed context → ad → capture → **continue your scroll**.  
**Ad job:** make one-tap **output legible** — never persuade. Hypothesis: if they understand what they receive, a meaningful share taps; non-tappers self-select out (data). Instrument two failure modes: don’t understand vs understand and don’t tap.  
**Pre-frame:** ad must establish that an agent will follow / prepare — else first text reads as spam.  
**Post-capture surface:** continue scroll — agent comes to them (not a thank-you dashboard).

### 6.3 Activation input contract (finish line)

| Input | Notes |
|-------|--------|
| Authorization / authentication into **firm database** (or equivalent that makes the campaign real) | Hard; after demonstration |
| Acceptance of payment terms — **escrow** | Contingent; one presented door |

**Unbudgeted.** Agent walks beside them.

**Forward-deploy (∈ activation, not acquisition):**

- After acquisition inputs land: scrape **public firm facts**, instantiate from **existing Om Coda templates** (launch → re-engagement → reactivation — methodology is Om Coda’s, **not** derived from their client list).
- Serve **no-login prepared workspace** + agent text walkthrough / deep links.
- Positioning: **“I prepared this campaign,”** not “look at our platform.”
- Firm identity = authentication / branding detail — **not** a claim we already have their clients.
- Marginal cost ≈ scrape + compute (agent presents; automation executes).
- Prepared workspace proves **readiness**; **value** proves via escrow + run.

# Systems — Goal (class = objective; goal = completion)

**Seat:** Systems Analyst.  
**Status:** Founder expansion 2026-08-15. Same grade as OPERATOR-REVISIONS: **denser than Seed/World, not Seed/World law until Story is promoted.** Founder: this is an expansion, not a trial balloon — will not be taken back.  
**Does not:** mint a table; overwrite the Agents flagship (PHASE-TWO-LOG 15:43 UTC); rewrite Seed/World.  
**Join:** [`SYSTEMS-STORY.md`](./SYSTEMS-STORY.md) §7 · [`OPERATOR-REVISIONS.md`](./OPERATOR-REVISIONS.md) §5c · [`guidelines/Reactivation.md`](../../guidelines/Reactivation.md) · SA log through **22:41 UTC grain lock** · UI-blueprint ascribe [`SYSTEMS-AGENTS-ASCRIBE.md`](./SYSTEMS-AGENTS-ASCRIBE.md). **Grain names:** more recent is current — **sequence contains campaigns**. 17:05 section below used the opposite words; witnessing only, not law.

Requirements must **not** extract a `goal` state from this file until Story §7 carries a promoted **must**. Until then this file is the substance so the detail is not background.

**2026-08-21 — the mechanism is settled (does not change the wording above).** Founder: objective met is *akin to a Local event* — this form filled and submitted by this user, detected, matched back to the sequence. Housing is therefore the event mechanism Tower already has: the completion write **is** the event; what was missing is the **instance axis on that row** (`fact_writebacks` had no persisted `form_ref`; sends carried no enrollment / campaign / objective). Cut: [`SYSTEMS-CHANGE-PACKET-022.md`](./SYSTEMS-CHANGE-PACKET-022.md). Consequence: the 15:43 escalation point (**other agent · other workflow · or it ends**) needs **no destination column and no `goal` table** — escalation is a **subscription** to `objective_met`. Story §7 promotion remains a wording must, not a structural one.

---

## Founder excerpts (do not paraphrase away)

Spoken 2026-08-15. Kept specific. Ellipses only where filler; no generated list.

**What a goal is**

> A goal is a completion of an objective.

> A goal is critical to creating any agent. Like you can't, and you can't even create the workflow without the goal.

> We need to define a certain, certain goals. … What are goals like on the system side of things, what could be goals?

**Sequence class = objective (three classes)**

> There are only really three types of like three classes of sequences. They could be called different things, but … the way we even class sequences is by their objective. The opt-in is not just a random sequence.

> To reactivation. Usually it's our re-engagement … the opt-ins last launch campaign is, or the sequence.

> Why does someone get an engagement? Well, because we want to get some data. It's data requests, I think for the most part.

> What is a reactivation? A reactivation is a meeting request.

**Mini-goals inside a class (opt-in named first)**

> It's not just a campaign goal because it has a series of things that we like check, check marks that must be met inside of the opt-in, which are kind of like mini goals. … If it doesn't already, I'm sure it exists. There are like a couple of mini goals. Actually, they are, you have to dig through the repo to find it.

**Correction of “no goal”**

> You said there's a goal. There is a goal, which is meeting books. … When it comes to other like re-engagement or there's no goal.

**Escalation is already many levels; goals-as-events emerge between campaigns**

> Within a sequence … you can create goals as escalations to the next thing.

> Escalations are so many different levels as escalation within nodes, as like attempt slash retries, like, oh, if email, email's criteria isn't met, okay, then text. These are like … attempt sequencing, right? Within attempt sequencing.

> Then you also have … the sequence completion … criteria or not criteria, but it could literally just be like a node or something.

> Agents allows you to not only create within like a nodes within an attempt, but I think it can also help you create a campaign. And within between campaigns, you can also have escalation points … one that definitely emerges is goals as escalation events.

**Durability (this file exists because of this)**

> I'm not gonna sit back and say, I don't want this. … There's no like time I'm gonna say, oh, no, that was a mistake. No, I'm expanding the idea. So it's probably something that should be marked down somehow. … At the minimum, log worthy, and you take very detailed, specific excerpts from it so that you don't miss that detail. You don't leave that detail in the background. It's critical.

---

## Systems reading (alignment, not a substitute flag)

| Founder clause | Systems meaning |
|---|---|
| Goal = **completion of an objective** | Not a vibe, not a metric flag, not the attempt ladder. A **done** on an objective. |
| Sequences are **classed by objective** | `seq_phase_order` / Story 7 phases **are** the three objectives: opt-in, re-engagement, reactivation. The calendar is how you pursue the objective, not the class. |
| Goal **required** to create an agent **and** a workflow | Authoring a package without naming its completion is incomplete. `workflow` and `sequence_template` have **no** goal/completion column today. |
| **Mini-goals** = checkmarks **inside** a class | Distinct from the class completion. Already in `guidelines/Reactivation.md` (quoted below). |
| Reactivation’s goal **is** meeting booked | Seed §4 / Story spine / system 12 / `meeting_booked`. Do not say “no goal.” |
| Re-engagement’s objective = **data request** | Story 8 `fact_ask` / `fact_writeback`; OPERATOR-REVISIONS §5b form submitted closes nudge. |
| Opt-in is not a random sequence | Waitlist then sign-up (guidelines). `consent_records.status` `waitlisted` \| `sequenced`. |
| Escalation **levels** (do not collapse) | (1) attempt sequencing inside a node (2) mini-goals (3) sequence/class completion (4) **between campaigns**, goal as **escalation event**. |
| Level 4 **definitely emerges** | Destinations already named on the 15:43 flagship: other agent · other workflow · or it ends. Once met, met. |

---

## Three class completions vs what is stood up

Story 7 + seeded `seq_phase_order`: **opt-in → re-engagement → reactivation**.

| Objective (class) | Completion (the goal) | Stood up | Not stood up |

# Magic / direct access link

**Date:** 2026-08-11  
**Status:** shipped on this branch — closes gap A in `APP-ELEVATION-GAP.md`

## Product intent

Invite is a **direct access URL**, not a login portal as the product.

- Open `/a/<token>` → one-time redeem → session cookie → `/prototype-ant`
- OTP `/login` remains as fallback

## Shape

| Piece | Path |
|-------|------|
| Table | `access_links` (`008_access_links.sql`) |
| Redeem | `POST /auth/access/redeem` `{ token }` → sets `tower_session` |
| Issue (auth) | `POST /auth/access/issue` — admin / self / `x-access-issue-secret` |
| Issue (wire) | `POST /wire/machine/access-invite` — mint + email from Provision |
| Provision | Returns `accessPath` (= `loginPath` when mint succeeds) |
| SPA entry | `/a/:token` → `AccessEntry` |

## TTL / consume

- 7 days (`ACCESS_LINK_TTL_MS`)
- One active link per user; re-issue invalidates prior
- Single-use: `consumed_at` on redeem

## Ops

```bash
npm run db:migrate   # applies 008_access_links.sql
npm run issue:access -- user@firm.com
npm run verify:access
```

Optional env:

- `PUBLIC_APP_URL` / `APP_ORIGIN` — absolute URL in invite emails
- `ACCESS_ISSUE_SECRET` — header `x-access-issue-secret` for scripted `POST /auth/access/issue`

## Deploy note (Vercel POST)

Auth/wire entries use `scripts/vercel-entries/fetchBridge.ts` (buffer body → `app.fetch`).  
The old `@hono/node-server/vercel` adapter left `c.req.json()` hanging (504) when the body stream was already drained — that blocked OTP and access redeem on production until this bridge.

# V2 backlog — Automations free-form graph walk

**v1 (shipped):** runtime recognizes and walks the **validated shape** only:

`Trigger → Constants → Conditions/Branch → Rules → Action → Exit`

The canvas is the editor for that shape’s parameters. Every drawable workflow in v1 is guaranteed runnable by construction when it follows this pipeline.

## Deferred to v2

- Walk **arbitrary** graphs (cycles, parallel fan-out/fan-in, multiple Actions, orphan islands).
- Full server-side evaluation of If/Rule expressions with the same fidelity as the client `resolveUpstreamInput` preview (v1 uses eligibility/context heuristics for Branch).
- Multi-trigger workflows with independent start nodes and join semantics.
- Visual debugger that steps node-by-node against live `workflow_run.node_status` mid-flight.
- Compiling non-validated shapes into a safe intermediate representation before execute.

Until then: reject or no-op graphs that are not validated shape (walker returns an error on `workflow_run`).
